name: CPA licensure pathway by state
description: Whether a state now licenses CPAs on a 120-credit-hour pathway (bachelor's degree plus one or two years of experience, no fifth year of school required) or still requires the traditional 150 credit hours, and the date the newer pathway took effect. Every state adopted 150 hours between the 1980s and 2000s; since Ohio HB 238 in July 2025, roughly half the states have passed a competing pathway that substitutes work experience for the extra 30 credit hours, an explicit response to the accounting profession's hiring shortage. A candidate deciding how many more credits to take, and a firm deciding whether an out-of-state hire is licensable, both need to know which rule applies in a specific state on a specific date -- and the two pathways can coexist with different experience and exam-eligibility requirements, so a single 'hours required' number is not enough. No federal body regulates CPA licensure; each state board of accountancy sets and amends its own rule, and the national umbrella body (NASBA) publishes the state list only as an image map and an embedded spreadsheet, not as extractable text.

records.pathway_status: there are now three pathways to licensure for candidates to choose from
records.source_quote: thanks to the passage of H0563 during the 2026 Legislative session, there are now three pathways to licensure for candidates to choose from. These new pathways will be available beginning July 1, 2026.

records.credit_hours_for_licensure: Baccalaureate or higher degree; total education must include an accounting concentration
records.source_quote: Pathway 3 – Baccalaureate or higher degree; total education must include an accounting concentration and two (2) years of qualifying experience.

records.pathway_status: there will be a new pathway to licensure as a CPA
records.credit_hours_for_licensure: a baccalaureate degree and 2 years’ experience
records.source_quote: The Mississippi State Board of Public Accountancy is pleased to advise that effective July 1, 2026, there will be a new pathway to licensure as a CPA! This new pathway will require a baccalaureate degree and 2 years’ experience. The old pathway of a baccalaureate degree with additional hours up to 150 semester hours and 1 year experience is still acceptable.

records.pathway_status: a baccalaureate degree with a concentration in accounting
records.credit_hours_for_licensure: a baccalaureate degree with a concentration in accounting
records.source_quote: a baccalaureate degree with a concentration in accounting as required by ARM 201.501 and two years of accounting experience meeting the requirements of ARM 24.201.502

records.pathway_status: Pathway 3: Bachelor’s Degree and Two Years of Experience
records.credit_hours_for_licensure: Earn a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university
records.experience_requirement: Complete at least 4,000 hours of qualifying experience over a period of at least two years, but no more than six years.
records.source_quote: Pathway 3: Bachelor’s Degree and Two Years of Experience Earn a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university; and Complete at least 4,000 hours of qualifying experience over a period of at least two years, but no more than six years.

records.pathway_status: A bachelor’s degree with an accounting concentration and two years of relevant experience
records.credit_hours_for_licensure: A bachelor’s degree with an accounting concentration
records.source_quote: A bachelor’s degree with an accounting concentration and two years of relevant experience, or A master’s degree with an accounting concentration and one year of relevant experience

records.pathway_status: Bachelor’s only pathway – minimum of two (2) years; Master’s degree or 150 semester hour pathway - minimum of one year.
records.experience_requirement: Bachelor’s only pathway – minimum of two (2) years
records.source_quote: This does not change under Senate Bill 797 (2025). Effectively that means that the exact same requirements of who qualifies as a supervisor toward licensure, and what the competencies toward licensure are, are not proposed to change in any way, except solely with respect to the minimum length of supervision depending on the pathway chosen. (Bachelor’s only pathway – minimum of two (2) years; Master’s degree or 150 semester hour pathway - minimum of one year.)
